d1_objective: The learner sees a fixed-amplitude tone rotate through phase, watches its in-phase and quadrature projections trade value, finds the phase where a sine-only amplitude estimate vanishes, and then sees the I/Q magnitude and wrapped phase remain correct across the entire phase family.

sources.lesson_status: No lesson.mdx exists at preflight time; the lesson author must place the guided sine-null-then-I/Q task beside the embed without changing this numerical contract.

targets.lesson_embed_owned_by_lesson_author: <Demo name="QuadratureDetectorLab" caption="Find a phase that nulls the sine-only detector, then switch to I/Q and verify amplitude and wrapped phase over the full phase sweep." />

implementation_contract.export: default function QuadratureDetectorLab() with no required props
implementation_contract.client_boundary: Put "use client" before imports because this narrow component owns useState and event handlers. Import only useState and the existing UI kit; keep all constants, projection math, seeded-phase logic, sweep checks, and SVG geometry in the same client module. No props cross the boundary.
implementation_contract.lazy_loading: Add only the explicit registry import promise. DemoHost already constructs React.lazy loaders once at module scope and owns Suspense; do not add next/dynamic, another lazy/Suspense layer, ssr:false, or a variable import path.
implementation_contract.styling: Use existing Tailwind utilities and app theme tokens. Use currentColor for SVG axes/text; house amber #e2903a for I/cosine and blue #4c8dd6 for Q/sine, with labels, line styles, and outlines as non-color cues. Add no CSS module, global CSS, inline stylesheet, or chart library.

signal_and_math.record: x[n]=A cos(omega0 n + phi), n=0,...,19, with A=1, omega0=0.3 pi rad/sample=0.15 cycles/sample. Twenty samples contain exactly three cycles.
signal_and_math.units: n is a dimensionless sample index; omega0 is radians/sample; phi is displayed in degrees and converted internally to radians.

projections.I: (2/N) sum from n=0 to N-1 of x[n] c[n] = A cos(phi)
projections.Q: -(2/N) sum from n=0 to N-1 of x[n] s[n] = A sin(phi)
projections.sign_reason: The negative sine correlation makes I+jQ=A exp(j phi) for x[n]=A cos(omega0 n+phi).

signal_and_math.orthogonality_contract: Because omega0=2 pi*3/20, sum cos^2=sum sin^2=N/2 and sum sin cos=0. Therefore the displayed equalities and I/Q recovery hold for every real phi in exact arithmetic; the result is not generalized to arbitrary finite windows or off-bin frequencies.

sine_only_estimator.nulls: phi=0 degrees and +/-180 degrees modulo 360, where Q=0 although A=1

iq_estimator.phase_degrees: phihat=atan2(Q,I)*180/pi, normalized to the canonical interval (-180,180], with -180 displayed as +180
iq_estimator.zero_magnitude_rule: Phase is undefined when Ahat_IQ is zero. The declared benchmark A=1 avoids that degenerate case; the readout still names the rule.

thresholds.full_phase_pass: Both strict inequalities hold on the deterministic -180 to +180 degree implementation sweep at 0.25-degree spacing, while the orthogonality identity supplies the all-real-phase mathematical guarantee.
thresholds.sine_null_falsification: Detector mode is sine-only, abs(Q)<1e-12, and sine-only relative amplitude error>0.99. The readout says FALSIFIED rather than treating the null as absence of a tone.

derived_only: 20 samples, I, Q, sine-only and I/Q estimates, errors, null/pass booleans
phasor, projection, detector-bar, and sample-stem SVG geometry

The sine-only amplitude estimate is 0.601815, so its relative error is 39.8185%, while the paired magnitude is 1 and paired phase is 37 degrees. The first screenshot already demonstrates phase sensitivity without starting at the final null.

controls: PresetGroup labelled Detector, with Sine only and I/Q pair.
PresetGroup labelled Phase cases, with the four named phase presets; activeIndex clears after a manual/random phase leaves a preset.

Button labelled New seeded phase. Advance seed=(imul(seed,1664525)+1013904223)>>>0, then set phaseDeg=round(seed/2^32*360-180). The deterministic initial sequence is -176, 58, -66, 176, 47, 103 degrees.
Slider labelled input phase phi, min -180, max 180, step 1, display degrees and expose the same value via aria-valuetext.
guided_task: Start in Sine only and use presets, the slider, or seeded trials to observe that its amplitude estimate changes with phase.
Find Sine null 0 degrees; TargetList and Readout report Q approximately zero, 100% amplitude error, and FALSIFIED.
Switch to I/Q pair; the current estimate reports amplitude one and the correct wrapped phase.
Read the full-sweep maximum errors and obtain PASS only when both strict thresholds hold.
state_and_interaction.feedback_budget: Each live update performs 20 sample/projection operations and simple SVG mapping. The 1,441-phase by 20-sample deterministic sweep is computed once at module initialization (28,820 samples), requires no memoization/effect, and remains far below 200 ms.

readouts_and_visual.kit_composition: Panel outer container; two PresetGroups; one Button; one Slider; one TargetList; one Readout. Every control/live region comes from components/ui; no new primitive is needed.
target_list: Find the sine-only null: live Q, Ahat_sine, and relative amplitude error; met only at the declared falsification condition.
I/Q passes every phase: dense-sweep maximum amplitude and phase errors; met only in I/Q mode when both strict limits pass.
readout_fields: A=1, omega0=0.3 pi rad/sample=0.15 cycles/sample, N=20
I and Q to six decimals
active estimator amplitude and relative error
I/Q wrapped phase estimate and error, or 'phase unavailable' for sine only
PASS/Not yet and explicit FALSIFIED message at the one-projection null
full-sweep maximum amplitude and wrapped-phase error
readouts_and_visual.visual: Dependency-free responsive DOM/SVG. Use a two-column grid at sm and one column at 360px: a unit-circle phasor panel with labelled I and Q drop projections, and a detector panel with side-by-side sine-only |Q| and I/Q hypot(I,Q) bars against a dashed true-A=1 line. Below, a full-width 20-sample stem plot of x[n] updates with phase. In sine-only mode the unmeasured I leg is dashed/muted and the sine bar has the active outline; in I/Q mode both legs and the paired bar are active. Never connect discrete sample dots.
readouts_and_visual.non_color_cues: I and Q are directly labelled; sine-only uses one projection and an active outline, I/Q uses a vector/bracket and a different active outline; true amplitude is dashed; PASS, FALSIFIED, numeric values, filled/hollow points, and solid/dashed strokes carry every conclusion without color.
readouts_and_visual.theme: Use currentColor and opacity for axes, labels, guides, inactive marks, and stems; amber/blue only as labelled semantic accents; var(--panel) for hollow marks. No hard-coded light background.
readouts_and_visual.mobile: Preset buttons wrap; controls stack; each upper SVG occupies full mobile width instead of shrinking a desktop two-panel canvas; waveform SVG remains fluid; labels are at least 12 user units and no element needs horizontal scroll at 360px.

accessibility.keyboard: PresetGroup and Button render native buttons; Slider renders a native range input. Tab, Enter/Space, and arrow keys cover the full task; no pointer-only gesture.
accessibility.touch: Existing Button min-h-11 and Slider h-11 provide at least 44px targets; rows wrap and remain separated on narrow screens.
accessibility.aria: Wrap both preset groups in labelled role=group regions. Give Button and Slider explicit labels/units. TargetList and Readout announce live status politely. Each SVG has role=img and a dynamic aria-label naming phase, I, Q, active detector estimate, current error, and pass/falsification status.
accessibility.motion: No timer or animation; input replaces static geometry synchronously, so reduced-motion users lose nothing.
accessibility.theme_and_contrast: Verify both themes manually; no information relies only on amber versus blue.

deterministic_checks: At phi=90 degrees: I is within 8e-17 of zero, Q=0.9999999999999997, and the sine-only amplitude happens to pass; the interface must still state that one scalar cannot identify arbitrary phase.
At phi=0 degrees: I=1.0000000000000002, abs(Q)<2e-16, Ahat_sine approximately zero with 100% error, and Ahat_IQ=1 with phihat approximately 0; falsification is true.

At phi=180 degrees: I=-1.0000000000000002, abs(Q)<2e-16, canonical I/Q phase is +180 degrees, circular phase error is zero rather than 360 degrees, and the second sine-only null is recognized. An input endpoint of -180 degrees represents the same phase and is displayed as +180 degrees.

Across 1,441 phases from -180 to 180 in 0.25-degree increments, the actual 20-sample dot-product implementation has maximum relative amplitude error 8.881784197001252e-16 and maximum wrapped phase error 0 degrees; both strict gates pass by wide margin.

The algebraic orthogonality identities establish the same I/Q result for every real phase, while the dense sweep is an implementation regression check rather than evidence for off-bin/general-window cases.
Changing detector mode never changes phase, seed, samples, I, or Q. Changing phase never changes A, omega0, N, or the full-sweep maxima.
Strict boundaries: exactly 1% amplitude error fails and exactly 2 degrees phase error fails; use <, not <=. Phase is never reported as meaningful if the recovered magnitude is zero.

loc_plan.strategy: Use compact module constants, one projection helper reused by live state and the sweep, map fixed sample/tick arrays, and keep only three state values. Do not extract runtime files, duplicate desktop/mobile SVGs, add a reducer/effect, or add a math/chart/random library.

validation_and_preview: Confirm the file begins with use client, default-exports a no-required-props component, imports only useState and @/components/ui, and is no more than 200 physical lines.
Run a deterministic Node/TypeScript harness for every numeric, wrap, threshold, seed-sequence, and all-phase assertion above.
After lesson.mdx embeds the demo, run npm run validate -- digital-signal-processing complex-sinusoids-and-phasors.
Use npm run preview for static light/dark lesson layout, expecting the nonhydrated placeholder, then npm run dev for the actual client interaction.

In development, inspect desktop and 360px in both themes; keyboard-select every detector/preset, arrow the phase slider through -180/0/180, use seeded trials, verify activeIndex clearing, reproduce null/PASS moments, and check for hydration warnings, clipping, horizontal scroll, stale live text, or color-only meaning.

checklist_expectation.D3: PASS: the 37-degree initial state is nondegenerate and already shows one-projection bias; four named phase presets anchor the task.
checklist_expectation.D4: PASS: the learner can reach an explicit FALSIFIED null and then a separate strict all-phase PASS.
checklist_expectation.D5: PASS by plan: one 196-line default-exported client component, existing UI kit only, zero dependencies, native keyboard/touch controls, and responsive theme-safe visuals.
